page: Amazon Web Services m7a.8xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9R14 processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz with a single thread per core. The hardware configuration includes 128.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance operates on the Nitro hypervisor and does not include local storage or GPU accelerators. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 12 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks place the m7a.8xlarge in the top 25% for both single-core and multi-core CPU stress tests. The AMD EPYC processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and cryptography extensions like AES and SHA_NI, contributing to strong results in Passmark CPU encryption and extended instruction tests. Memory performance is mixed; read-only bandwidth for small cached blocks is in the top 25%, whereas large-block uncached read bandwidth falls into the middle 50%. In application-specific benchmarks, the instance demonstrates strong performance in Redis SET operations, software compilation, and database operations, while static web serving throughput remains average.

For machine learning workloads, the instance achieves top-tier performance in prompt processing for small 135M parameter models, though performance scales down to average for larger 70B models. Given the dedicated CPU allocation and high-speed DDR5 memory, the m7a.8xlarge offers a balanced resource density for general-purpose workloads. It is well-suited for database operations, software compilation, medium-scale LLM inference, and compute-intensive applications that benefit from dedicated physical cores without requiring local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration.
